selection.method: uniform random.sample of ten active Sarj-owned source/test catalog rules per round; replacement between rounds

admissions.reproduction: A literal U+2028 inside one shell comment moves the shfmt diagnostic from physical line 2 to reported line 3; deleting a trailing blank line reports line 1 instead of the changed suffix.
admissions.gap: str.splitlines recognizes separators that are shell data, and zip omits unequal suffix lengths.
admissions.harm: CI and editor locations point to a different physical source line and byte coordinate pair.
admissions.invalidStateVersusPreference: Diagnostic coordinates must match the physical source; no formatting preference or new detector is added.
admissions.smallestFix: Use stdlib LF-preserving line iteration and zip_longest in the canonical formatter diagnostic boundary.

admissions.reproduction: Compose command [bash, -Z, -c, 'printf unsafe'] yields no ShellCheck or shfmt report despite an unproven known-shell invocation.
admissions.gap: The shared interpreter grammar returns unknown, but the shell projection owner handles that result as a foreign interpreter skip.
admissions.harm: Malformed or unproven supported-shell argv is indistinguishable from successful clean coverage.
admissions.invalidStateVersusPreference: Unproven supported-shell execution must fail coverage; source semantics and valid foreign interpreter exclusions stay with their existing owners.
admissions.smallestFix: Raise ProgramProjectionError for unknown invocations only when the executable is a currently supported shell.

admissions.reproduction: redundant-class-docstring and redundant-docstring contain six identical helpers and each computes the same runtime-consumption alias closure for one PythonFileContext.
admissions.gap: The normal combined runner repeats deterministic broad AST analysis and maintains two copies of the same semantics.
admissions.harm: Extra per-file work and divergent future fixes for runtime-observed docstrings.
admissions.invalidStateVersusPreference: Implementation-only consolidation; diagnostic sets, exclusions, severity and rule IDs must remain identical.
admissions.smallestFix: Move the unchanged consumption analysis to the existing docstring helper owner and cache an immutable frozenset lazily per file context.

admissions.reproduction: Pinned shfmt 3.14.1 changes printf '%s' before\vafter from one data argument into two, and converts form-feed comment data into a new executable line; native Bash stdout differs before/after while the current fix guard permits both writes.
admissions.owner: sarj_standards.libs.linting.shell_format.validate_format_fix, shared by standalone and embedded planning
admissions.gap: The existing native byte-removal guard protects carriage returns only, while Bash also treats vertical tabs and form feeds as literal data rather than spaces or LF.
admissions.harm: An automatic formatting fix can change argument bytes or start executing previously commented text.
admissions.invalidStateVersusPreference: Reject behavior-changing native rewrites; do not ban valid source characters or introduce a style rule. Formatting checks remain available.
admissions.smallestFix: Extend the existing byte-loss check to carriage return, vertical tab and form feed; retain atomic planning and original source bytes when refusing a fix.

seededCorpus.classification: all four findings are seeded name-only unconsumed docstrings, true positives

docstringAnalysis.method: Four interleaved before/after process pairs, AB BA AB BA; identical interpreter and dependencies, baseline restores four affected Python modules; seven warm/combined samples and seven fresh child processes per process.
docstringAnalysis.combinedRunner: sarj_python_lint.__main__.check_source with the two affected rules and one shared PythonFileContext
docstringAnalysis.baselineLoading: Four affected modules are restored through a package namespace overlay. Hot combined timing excludes import setup; cold timings include that loader overhead and cannot isolate the optimization alone.

formatterPosition.method: Eight interleaved in-process pairs per fixture, ordinary LF controls; compares the unchanged diagnostic construction except its line boundary handling. Correctness fixes are measured separately from docstring optimization.

reproductionCommands: code-standards --root . maintain rules changes --before origin/main --after HEAD
limitations: This is a reproducible machine-assisted source/test review with native example execution; deep manual analysis and adversarial probes focus on admitted candidates, not a claim of exhaustive manual review of every selected rule.
Repeated selections reuse evidence; 300 draws are not 300 distinct rules or independent semantic coverage.
Native example counts do not imply independent coverage; equivalent execution contracts can repeat across examples.
Only already-local repositories were scanned. Python selection is the first 250 sorted eligible tracked paths per repository, not an unbiased full-repository sample.
The unseeded Python corpus has zero findings; unchanged zero counts are not correctness evidence. Eight separately pinned seeded files establish positive and negative behavior.
Legacy shebangs containing vertical tabs retain native analysis, while their byte-removing fixes now require manual review.
The native byte-loss guard is conservative: rewrites that remove protected bytes require manual review even if a future formatter could encode equivalent data safely.
Performance is fixture-specific. Combined timing covers the two affected rules; cold process startup and memory differences are observational, not universal improvements.
One pre-existing native formatter failure remains in the shell corpus. Before/after native finding and formatter aggregate counts are equal.

Ash and BusyBox argv integration remains outside the supported adapter contract; expansion is deferred until native option and applet boundaries are proven. No duplicate ShellCheck detectors are introduced.
Private corpus source pins, identities, paths, snippets and finding tuples remain in owner-readable overlays; this artifact contains only public rule data and redacted aggregates.
